metadata.name: trellis_credits
metadata.description: Trellis prepaid, spend-only USDC inference credits

instructions.name: build_profile
docs: Anyone: the floors compiled into this binary (profile 0 = mainnet, 1 = devnet), as return data.

instructions.name: cancel_close
docs: Whoever asked for the closure, or the key's registered owner wallet: take a queued closure back while nothing has
been paid. The key may do this once per `KEY_CANCEL_COOLDOWN`. A depositor has no say over a closure.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Whoever asked for the closure (the key itself, or the owner wallet), or the key's registered owner wallet.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the fee and, the first time the key cancels, the small rent of its `CloseGuard`. Any wallet.

accounts.name: guard
docs: When the key may next cancel. `init_if_needed`: created by the first cancel and never closed, so it cannot be
re-initialised to forget a cooldown.

instructions.name: close_account
docs: Signed by the key itself: close the key and queue a refund of the unspent balance to the wallets that funded it.

accounts.name: key
docs: The API key's own ed25519 keypair (derived from the secret). Its public key must hash to `key_hash`.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the RefundRequest rent and the fee (the key's keypair holds no SOL). Any wallet.

instructions.name: close_account_by_owner
docs: Signed by the key's registered owner wallet, without the key: close the key and queue the same refund. A closure
asked for this way cannot be cancelled with the key.

accounts.name: owner
docs: The key's registered owner wallet.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the RefundRequest rent and the fee. Any wallet (usually the owner itself).

instructions.name: commit_spent_root
docs: Settlement authority: commit the hour's spend root and advance `spent_total`.

accounts.name: spent_root
docs: One account per hour: a second commit for the same hour fails at `init`.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: Deposit USDC for `key_hash`; creates the credit account on first use and extends
`expires_at` to now + `credit_ttl`. Anyone may deposit to any key; it gives the depositor no rights over it.

accounts.name: credit
docs: Anyone may deposit to any key hash ("top up a key"). `init_if_needed` is justified here: a deposit is the only way a credit account comes
into existence (there is no separate "open" instruction, per Backend §5.1), and the
re-initialisation attack does not apply because this program never closes a
`CreditAccount` (closure sets `closed = true` and keeps the account).

accounts.name: share
docs: What this wallet has put into this key, and where it wants it back. `init_if_needed`: created by the wallet's
first deposit to the key and never closed, so it cannot be re-initialised.

instructions.name: init_config
docs: Upgrade authority only: creates the config, the vault and the outflow limiter.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Admin key (Squads 2-of-3 in production). Pays for the config and vault accounts. Must be the program's upgrade
authority, so nobody else can initialise the program between deploy and init.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Program-owned USDC vault; authority is the config PDA.

instructions.name: init_limiter
docs: Creates the outflow limiter for a config initialised before it existed (anyone may pay).

instructions.name: migrate_config
docs: Grows a config created by an earlier version to the current layout (anyone may pay; works once).

instructions.name: migrate_limiter
docs: Grows a limiter created by an earlier version to the current layout (anyone may pay; works once).

instructions.name: notice_expiry
docs: Settlement authority: start the grace period for an expired balance.

instructions.name: pay_refund
docs: Settlement authority: pay (part of) a queued refund to one depositor's destination, after the request's
`payable_at` and within the refund allowance.

accounts.name: share
docs: The share of one wallet that deposited to this key: the refund is that wallet's own USDC coming back.

instructions.name: propose_config
docs: Authority: record any config change (including an authority hand-over); it can be applied after
`CONFIG_TIMELOCK` (24h).

accounts.name: pending_config
docs: One pending change at a time: a second proposal fails at `init` until this one is applied or cancelled.

accounts.name: new_treasury
docs: Optional new treasury token account; must hold the configured USDC mint.

instructions.name: resolve_config
docs: `apply = true`: the authority installs the pending change after the timelock (a new authority must co-sign).
`apply = false`: the authority drops it (the guardian cannot); anyone may clear an expired one.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Applying or cancelling: the authority. Anyone may clear a proposal that has expired.

accounts.name: new_authority
docs: Required only when the pending change hands the authority over: the new authority must sign to take it.

instructions.name: set_deposits_paused
docs: Guardian or authority pauses new deposits for `PAUSE_TTL`; only the authority unpauses. Never affects outflows.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Either the guardian or the authority.

instructions.name: set_key_authority
docs: Register the key's owner wallet (signed by the key and by the wallet), or, once one is registered, change or
clear it (signed by the current owner; a new owner signs too). The key alone cannot change a registered owner.

accounts.name: signer
docs: While the key has no owner: the API key's own ed25519 keypair (its public key must hash to `key_hash`). Once an
owner is registered: that owner wallet. The key alone can never replace or clear a registered owner.

accounts.name: new_owner
docs: The wallet being registered as owner. It must sign: a key cannot name a wallet that has not agreed (and so
cannot borrow someone else's standing, security review round 3 R3-23). Omitted only when the owner clears itself.

instructions.name: set_refund_destination
docs: A depositor: name another USDC token account for its own refunds from this key.

accounts.name: refund_to
docs: The USDC token account the depositor wants its refunds from this key paid to.

instructions.name: set_settlements_paused
docs: Guardian or authority pauses spend commits, host settlement and sweeps for `PAUSE_TTL`; only the authority
unpauses. Closures and closure refunds are never paused.

accounts.name: signer
docs: The guardian or the authority may pause; only the authority may unpause.

instructions.name: settle_to_host
docs: Settlement authority: pay a host from the vault, bounded by committed spend and the per-window limit.

accounts.name: spent_root
docs: The committed hour this settlement references (must exist).

instructions.name: sweep_expired
docs: Settlement authority: move the unspent part of an expired, noticed balance to treasury after the grace period.

instructions.name: update_config
docs: Authority: tightening changes only, effective at once. Loosening is refused (`RequiresTimelock`).

types.name: BuildProfile
docs: What `build_profile` returns: the floors compiled into this binary.

fields.name: profile
docs: 0 = mainnet floors (the default build); 1 = the `devnet` cargo feature.

types.name: CloseCancelled
docs: A queued closure was withdrawn before anything was paid: the key is open again with its balance.

types.name: CloseGuard
docs: When the key itself may next cancel a closure. PDA `["close_guard", key_hash]`, created by the key's first cancel.
Two parties can hold the same API key (its owner and whoever it leaked to). Without this, one of them could take
every closure of the other back just before it became payable, for ever. The key may cancel one closure and then
none for `KEY_CANCEL_COOLDOWN`, which is longer than any refund delay: the next closure runs to payment. The
registered owner wallet is not bound by it.

types.name: CloseRequester
docs: Emitted with `CloseRequested`: who asked for the closure (the key's own address, or the key's registered owner
wallet). Only that party or the owner can cancel it. A separate event so that `CloseRequested` keeps its layout.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: After this the proposal can only be cancelled.

types.name: CreditAccount
docs: One per API key. PDA `["credit", key_hash]` where `key_hash = sha256(key address)` and the key address is the
ed25519 public key derived from the API key.
Spend is tracked off-chain and committed hourly as `SpentRoot`s, so `balance` is the
prepaid amount still on-chain, not the live remaining balance. There is no withdraw
instruction: the only outflows are `pay_refund` (closure), `settle_to_host` and
`sweep_expired`.

fields.name: authority
docs: The key's owner wallet, or the default pubkey when none is registered. Registered once with
`set_key_authority`, signed by the key AND by the wallet; from then on only that wallet can change or clear it
(the key alone cannot). The owner can ask for a closure without the key (`close_account_by_owner`) and can
cancel any closure of the key; a closure the owner asked for cannot be cancelled with the key. It gives no claim
on funds: refunds go back to the wallets that deposited. Depositing gives no way to become the owner.
(Accounts created before the TR-05 fix may carry their first depositor here: clear it on devnet by closing.)

fields.name: expires_at
docs: Latest deposit time + `credit_ttl`; every deposit extends the whole balance.

fields.name: expiry_notice_at
docs: Unix time of `notice_expiry`, or 0 if no notice is outstanding.

types.name: CreditsConfig
docs: Program configuration. Singleton PDA `["config"]`; also the signing authority of the vault.
`authority` is the admin key. In production this is a Squads 2-of-3 multisig; a single
pubkey is used until then. `settlement_authority` is the hot key of the settlement
service (commits spent roots, pays settlements and refunds, runs expiry). `guardian` can
only pause; it can never move funds.

fields.name: vault
docs: Token account PDA `["vault"]`, authority = this config PDA.

fields.name: treasury_token_account
docs: Destination for swept expired balances. Must be a token account of `usdc_mint`.

fields.name: credit_ttl
docs: Seconds a balance lives after the latest deposit (default 365 days, never below `MIN_CREDIT_TTL`).

fields.name: refund_delay
docs: Seconds between `close_account` and the earliest `pay_refund` (default 72h, never below `MIN_REFUND_DELAY`).

fields.name: expiry_grace
docs: Seconds between `notice_expiry` and the earliest `sweep_expired` (default 30 days, never below `MIN_EXPIRY_GRACE`).

fields.name: spent_total
docs: Cumulative spend committed via `commit_spent_root`. Upper bound for host settlement.

fields.name: settled_total
docs: Cumulative USDC paid out to hosts via `settle_to_host`. Never exceeds `spent_total`.

fields.name: latest_hour
docs: Last hour committed; hours must strictly increase.

fields.name: deposits_paused
docs: True while a deposit pause is set. It is in force only until `deposits_paused_until` (see `pause_active`).

fields.name: deposits_paused_until
docs: When the deposit pause lapses by itself (`PAUSE_TTL` after it was last set). 0 on a config that never paused.

fields.name: deposits_guardian_ready_at
docs: The guardian may not pause deposits again before this time (`GUARDIAN_PAUSE_COOLDOWN` after its last pause
was due to lapse).

types.name: DepositorShare
docs: What one wallet has deposited to one key, and where that wallet wants it back. PDA `["share", key_hash, depositor]`.
A closure refund never goes anywhere the key chooses (security re-review RR-05): it is paid back to the wallets
that funded the key, each at most what it put in, to the token account that wallet named. `refund_to` starts as the
token account the first deposit came from and only `depositor` can change it (`set_refund_destination`). Holding
the API key gives no way to redirect a balance, and depositing to someone's key gives no claim on anything but the
depositor's own USDC.

fields.name: refund_to
docs: USDC token account this depositor's refunds are paid to.

fields.name: deposited
docs: Cumulative USDC this wallet deposited to the key.

fields.name: refunded
docs: Cumulative USDC refunded to this wallet from the key. Never exceeds `deposited`.

fields.name: paused_until
docs: When the pause lapses by itself (0 when `paused` is false).

fields.name: max_balance_per_key
docs: 0 selects `DEFAULT_MAX_BALANCE_PER_KEY`.

fields.name: credit_ttl
docs: `None` selects the defaults (365 days, 72h, 30 days). A value outside the program's floors is rejected.

types.name: OutflowCapSet
docs: The absolute bound on one window's outflow (each of the two allowances), as it stands after a config change.

types.name: PendingConfig
docs: A loosening config change waiting out `CONFIG_TIMELOCK`. PDA `["pending_config"]`; one at a time.

fields.name: new_treasury
docs: Replacement treasury token account (mint-checked at proposal), if any.

types.name: RefundDestinationSet
docs: A depositor named another token account for its refunds from one key.

fields.name: depositor
docs: The wallet whose deposits this refund returns.

types.name: RefundRequest
docs: Queued closure refund. PDA `["refund", key_hash]`. Created by `close_account` (signed by the key) or
`close_account_by_owner` (signed by the key's registered owner wallet), removed again by `cancel_close` while nothing
has been paid.

fields.name: amount
docs: The key's on-chain balance when it was closed: the most that can ever be refunded.

fields.name: payable_at
docs: Earliest `pay_refund`: `requested_at` plus the refund delay AS IT WAS when the key was closed. A later change of
the delay does not move a request that is already queued (security re-review RR-10).

fields.name: paid_amount
docs: Cumulative amount paid so far; `pay_refund` may be called more than once and never pays more than `amount`.

fields.name: paid
docs: True once `paid_amount == amount`.

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: Who paid this account's rent; gets it back if the closure is cancelled.

fields.name: requested_by
docs: Who asked for this closure: the key's own address or the owner wallet. Only this party, or the owner, can
cancel it (security review round 3, R3-06).

types.name: SettleLimiter
docs: Outflow limiter. Singleton PDA `["limiter_v2"]`.
Two independent allowances, one for `settle_to_host` and one for `pay_refund`, so host payouts can never use up
what refunds may take and refunds can never hold up host payouts. Each is a continuously refilled allowance
(`refill_allowance`), not a bucket that resets: the cap of one `SETTLE_WINDOW` is `window_cap(base)`, at most
`SETTLE_BURST_BPS` of it can be held at once, and the rest arrives evenly over the window. Over ANY interval of one
window the outflow is therefore at most the cap; there is no boundary to straddle (security re-review RR-01).
The cap has two bounds (security review round 3, R3-07):
- a share (`rate_bps`) of `base`, and `base` is never more than the LOWEST balance the vault has had over the last
`SETTLE_WINDOW`. A deposit therefore counts only once it has been in the vault for a whole window: whoever holds
the settlement key cannot raise the cap by depositing and paying one unit, as it could when the base was the
balance after the previous payment;
- `cap_per_window`, an absolute amount set by the authority. Capital that sits in the vault long enough does raise
the share; this number it cannot raise.
How `base` is kept without touching `deposit`: every instruction that can lower the vault (`settle_to_host`,
`pay_refund`, `sweep_expired`) and `commit_spent_root` record the balance they leave behind (`last_vault`). Between
two of them the vault can only rise, so the lowest balance of any stretch is the one recorded at its start.
`base_cur` is the lowest balance of the current epoch (`now / SETTLE_WINDOW`), starting from `last_vault` when the
epoch is first seen; `base_prev` that of the epoch before (`last_vault` when nothing was recorded in it). The base
is `min(base_prev, base_cur, vault now)`, and any stretch of one window lies inside those two epochs.
`paused` (in force until `paused_until`) stops `commit_spent_root`, `settle_to_host` and `sweep_expired`. It never
stops deposits, closures or closure refunds.

fields.name: settle_allowance
docs: What `settle_to_host` may still pay right now (as of `settle_refilled_at`).

fields.name: base_cur
docs: The lowest vault balance seen in epoch `base_epoch` (in the earlier layout: the balance after the last payout).

fields.name: refund_allowance
docs: What `pay_refund` may still pay right now (as of `refund_refilled_at`).

fields.name: base_prev
docs: The lowest vault balance of the epoch before `base_epoch` (in the earlier layout: the balance after the last
refund).

fields.name: paused_until
docs: When the settlement pause lapses by itself (`PAUSE_TTL` after it was last set).

fields.name: guardian_pause_ready_at
docs: The guardian may not pause settlements again before this time.

fields.name: base_epoch
docs: The epoch (`unix time / SETTLE_WINDOW`) `base_cur` belongs to.

fields.name: last_vault
docs: The vault balance left behind by the last instruction that recorded it.

fields.name: cap_per_window
docs: The absolute bound on one window's outflow, for each of the two allowances. Never below `SETTLE_WINDOW_FLOOR`.

fields.name: paused_until
docs: When the pause lapses by itself (0 when `paused` is false).

types.name: SpentRoot
docs: Hourly commitment of off-chain spend. PDA `["spent_root", hour]`.
`root` is a sha256 Merkle root over the hour's spend records (leaf = sha256(sha256(bytes)),
node = sha256(min(a,b) || max(a,b)); see `trellis_anchor`).

types.name: SpentTotalWrittenDown
docs: `spent_total` was written down to `settled_total` (a timelocked repair).

types.name: UpdateConfigParams
docs: The fields `update_config` / `propose_config` may change. `None` leaves a field as it is.

fields.name: new_authority
docs: Hand the authority over. Only through the timelock, and the new authority must sign the apply.

fields.name: settle_rate_bps
docs: Share of the vault `settle_to_host` may pay per window, in bps (at most `MAX_SETTLE_RATE_BPS`).

fields.name: write_down_spent
docs: Write `spent_total` down to `settled_total`: the repair for a spent root that committed spend which never
happened (security re-review RR-06). Only through the timelock.

fields.name: outflow_cap_per_window
docs: The absolute bound on one window's outflow (each allowance). Lowering is immediate, raising goes through the
timelock; never below `SETTLE_WINDOW_FLOOR`.

constants.name: CONFIG_SEED
docs: PDA seeds.
| Account            | Seeds                                   | Owner / notes                              |
| `CreditsConfig`    | `["config"]`                            | singleton; signs vault transfers           |
| vault              | `["vault"]`                             | SPL token account, authority = config      |
| `CreditAccount`    | `["credit", key_hash]`                  | one per API-key hash                       |
| `SpentRoot`        | `["spent_root", hour.to_le_bytes()]`    | one per hour; second init fails            |
| `RefundRequest`    | `["refund", key_hash]`                  | one per closed key                         |
| `SettleLimiter`    | `["limiter_v2"]`                        | singleton; outflow rate limits and pause   |
| `DepositorShare`   | `["share", key_hash, depositor]`        | what one wallet deposited to one key       |
| `PendingConfig`    | `["pending_config"]`                    | a loosening config change waiting its delay|
| `CloseGuard`       | `["close_guard", key_hash]`             | when the key may next cancel a closure     |

constants.name: DEFAULT_CREDIT_TTL
docs: Credits expire 12 months after the latest deposit (Backend §5.1).

constants.name: DEFAULT_EXPIRY_GRACE
docs: Expired balances move to treasury only 30 days after the expiry notice.

constants.name: DEFAULT_MAX_BALANCE_PER_KEY
docs: USDC has 6 decimals: 5,000 USDC.

constants.name: DEFAULT_REFUND_DELAY
docs: Closure refunds wait 72h for the open-dispute check before they can be paid.

constants.name: LIMITER_SEED
docs: The limiter that replaced the fixed 24h bucket (security re-review RR-01) lives at a new address: the first
limiter's account (`["limiter"]`) has another layout and is no longer read by any instruction.

constants.name: MAX_BALANCE_PER_KEY_LIMIT
docs: The compiled maximum of `max_balance_per_key` while the programs are unaudited: 5,000 USDC. `init_config`,
`update_config` and `propose_config` refuse a higher value, so no key can raise the per-key cap above the published
figure; that takes a program upgrade (security review round 3). The same in the `devnet` build.

constants.name: MIN_DEPOSIT
docs: The smallest deposit: 1 USDC. A deposit creates a `DepositorShare` that a closure has to screen, read and pay, and
it cancels an expiry notice; below this a stranger could queue work in front of a key's owner for dust (R3-22).
